title: Tokens, Vectors, and Transformers · Level 2
slo: Explain how text is prepared and represented for a transformer model.

exercises.question_text: In a vocabulary, what does a token ID identify?

options.rationale: An ID is assigned to a distinct vocabulary token. Each occurrence of that token uses the same ID.
A token can appear at multiple positions. Its ID remains associated with its vocabulary identity.
options.better_fit: Use positional encoding for a token occurrence's location.

options.rationale: A dimension is one value inside a vector. A token ID identifies a vocabulary entry.
options.better_fit: Use this for an individual numeric value in a vector.

options.rationale: A decoder prediction selects a likely token. An ID labels tokens available in the vocabulary.
options.better_fit: Use this for the likely next token selected by a decoder.

exercises.explanation: Correct. A token ID identifies one distinct vocabulary token.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The preparation sequence would be out of order.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Assign vectors first, add position information, then send the prepared tokens onward.

exercises.correct_answer: Assign random vectors add positional encoding then send tokens into the transformer
exercises.explanation: Initial representations are assigned, order information is added, and the prepared representations are sent to the transformer.

exercises.question_text: The model architecture with an encoder block and decoder layer is a ___.

parts.text: The model architecture with an encoder block and decoder layer is a

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The answer would name a component or representation rather than the architecture.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: The full architecture containing encoder and decoder parts is a transformer.

exercises.explanation: A transformer contains encoder and decoder components and processes token representations.

exercises.question_text: A developer prepares a sentence containing two occurrences of "a" and must preserve their different locations. Which choices should the developer make? Select all that apply.

options.text: Reuse the same token ID for both
options.rationale: Both occurrences are the same vocabulary token. They therefore use the same assigned ID.

options.text: Give each occurrence a different position
options.rationale: The occurrences appear at different places in the sequence. Their positional information must differ.

options.text: Apply positional encoding to each occurrence
options.rationale: Each occurrence needs order information. Positional encoding provides this information.

options.text: Create a new vocabulary token for the second occurrence
options.error_type: Confuses repetition with a new token
options.rationale: A repeated occurrence is not a distinct vocabulary entry. It should reuse the known token ID.
options.better_fit: Use this only when the vocabulary gains a genuinely distinct token.

feedback.intrinsic: The vocabulary would grow without a new token being introduced.
feedback.instructional: Reuse the ID and use different positional encodings for the occurrences.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Identity stays the same while positional information changes.

exercises.question_text: In the word "unlikely," the piece "un" can be a ___ token.

parts.text: In the word "unlikely," the piece "un" can be a

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The answer would not name the kind of token represented by "un."
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: A sub-word is a token that represents part of a word.

exercises.explanation: Tokenization can break language into sub-word pieces, not only complete words.

exercises.question_text: A developer needs an architecture that turns token representations into contextual embeddings and then chooses the most probable next token. Which architecture should the developer choose?

options.rationale: A transformer creates embeddings and predicts likely next tokens. Its encoder and decoder support these tasks.
Tokenization splits text and assigns IDs. It does not create contextual embeddings or predict continuations.
options.better_fit: Use this to prepare the input before model processing.

feedback.intrinsic: The text would be prepared but no prediction architecture would be selected.
feedback.instructional: Tokenization prepares tokens; a transformer creates embeddings and predicts tokens.

options.rationale: Positional encoding supplies location information. It is not an encoder-decoder architecture.
options.better_fit: Use this alongside token representations when order matters.

feedback.intrinsic: Order would be available but the stated processing system would be absent.
feedback.instructional: Position conveys order; a transformer performs embedding and prediction work.

options.rationale: A system prompt guides behavior and constraints. It does not transform vectors or make next-token predictions.
options.better_fit: Use this to specify response behavior or tone.

feedback.intrinsic: Instructions alone would not provide the requested model computation.
feedback.instructional: Prompts guide behavior; transformer architecture processes and predicts tokens.

exercises.explanation: Correct. A transformer supplies both contextual representation and next-token prediction.

exercises.question_text: Put the processing steps in order.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: Prediction would incorrectly precede the representations it requires.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Place encoder work first, then decoder use of embeddings, then prediction.

exercises.correct_answer: Encoder creates embeddings decoder uses embeddings then decoder predicts the next token
exercises.explanation: Embeddings are created before the decoder uses them, and that use supports next-token prediction.

exercises.question_text: Arrange the parts to form a correct statement.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The rule for repeated vocabulary items would be unclear.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: State the repeated token first, then that it retains its assigned ID.

exercises.correct_answer: A repeated token keeps its assigned token ID
exercises.explanation: A token's identifier is reused whenever that vocabulary token appears.

exercises.question_text: A developer must split an incoming sentence into words, punctuation, and common character pieces before the model processes it. Which method should the developer choose?

options.rationale: Tokenization splits language into usable tokens. It is the required preparation step.
Positional encoding records where tokens occur. It does not create the token pieces.
options.better_fit: Use this after tokens are identified to represent sequence order.

feedback.intrinsic: The developer would have locations without first defining the pieces.
feedback.instructional: Choose tokenization to split the text; use positional encoding for order.

options.rationale: Embeddings are created from token representations in context. They do not perform the initial split.
options.better_fit: Use this when an encoder creates contextual vectors.

feedback.intrinsic: Processing would start before the input was divided into tokens.

options.error_type: Confuses input preparation with output generation
options.rationale: Prediction chooses a likely continuation. It does not prepare the supplied sentence.
options.better_fit: Use this when generating a response token.

feedback.intrinsic: The workflow would jump to generation too early.
feedback.instructional: Prepare input with tokenization before predicting output.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Tokenization produces the token pieces needed for later processing.

exercises.question_text: The individual numeric values in a vector are called ___.

parts.text: The individual numeric values in a vector are called

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The chosen term would not name one numeric element of a vector.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Token IDs identify tokens and embeddings are contextual vectors; individual values are dimensions.

exercises.explanation: A vector is made of numeric elements, each called a dimension.

exercises.question_text: A developer already has embeddings for a prompt and must predict its next most probable token. Which decoder capabilities should the developer use? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: The decoder uses encoder-created embeddings. They provide contextual representations for prediction.
The decoder uses attention while predicting. Attention helps it consider relevant sequence context.
The decoder uses a feed-forward neural network. It contributes to choosing a probable candidate.

options.text: New token IDs for each word
options.rationale: Token IDs are assigned during tokenization. The decoder predicts using embeddings, attention, and a feed-forward network.
options.better_fit: Use this only when assigning IDs to distinct vocabulary tokens.

feedback.intrinsic: Vocabulary identities would be changed instead of using prediction components.
feedback.instructional: For prediction, use embeddings, attention, and a feed-forward neural network; do not assign new IDs.

exercises.explanation: Correct. The decoder uses embeddings, attention, and a feed-forward neural network to predict the next token.

exercises.question_text: A developer represents the token "heard" as [2, 15, 1] to encode language and meaning attributes. What should the developer call this representation?

options.rationale: The representation is an array of numeric values. Such an array can encode token attributes.
A token ID is one integer for a vocabulary entry. The displayed representation has several numeric values.
options.better_fit: Use this for the single integer assigned to "heard" in the vocabulary.

feedback.intrinsic: The array's dimensions would be reduced to one identifier.
feedback.instructional: An array such as [2, 15, 1] is a token vector, not a token ID.

options.rationale: Positional encoding represents sequence location. The array in this scenario represents token attributes.
options.better_fit: Use this to indicate where "heard" occurs in the sentence.

feedback.intrinsic: The token's representation would be confused with its location.
feedback.instructional: Position shows order; a token vector encodes attributes.

options.rationale: A completion is generated language. A numeric array is a representation used by the model.
options.better_fit: Use this for text produced after next-token prediction.

feedback.intrinsic: Numeric data would incorrectly be treated as generated language.
feedback.instructional: Vectors represent tokens; completions are generated sequences.

exercises.explanation: Correct. The numeric array is a token vector.
